title: Prediction of 123I-FP-CIT SPECT Results from First Acquired Projections Using Artificial Intelligence.
summary: A CNN using the first two native DaT-SPECT projections and age classified full-scan normal/abnormal status in an independent 100-scan test set (49/50 abnormal cases detected); this supports a specific short-acquisition diagnostic prediction result, with false positives and threshold-dependent specificity.
ai_technology: A CNN uses only the initial two un-reconstructed SPECT projections plus age to infer the full-scan normal/abnormal category.

evidence.tested: Primary Methods specify the two-projection input, conservative binary labels and prespecified independent test set; Results report 49 true positives, 1 false negative, 26 true negatives, 24 false positives, 98% sensitivity and 52% specificity at the selected threshold.
evidence.unknown: A CNN using the first two native DaT-SPECT projections and age classified full-scan normal/abnormal status in an independent 100-scan test set (49/50 abnormal cases detected); this supports a specific short-acquisition diagnostic prediction result, with false positives and threshold-dependent specificity. An a-priori independent test set of 100 scans was withheld from training and validation; performance is threshold-sensitive, with 52% specificity, and external-site testing is not reported.
evidence.ai_role: A CNN uses only the initial two un-reconstructed SPECT projections plus age to infer the full-scan normal/abnormal category.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
